'''Su Qiang''' ({{zh|c=|s=苏锵|t=蘇鏘|p=Sū Qiāng|w=Su Ch'iang}}; 1931–2017) was a Chinese inorganic chemist. A pioneer in rare earth research and applications, he was elected an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news2.sysu.edu.cn/news01/149169.htm|title=沉痛悼念苏锵院士|website=Sun Yat-sen University|language=Chinese}}</ref>

Su enrolled at [[Sun Yat-sen University]] in 1948, he transferred to Department of Chemical Engineering (which is a part of Tianjin University nowadays), Peking University two years later, and graduated in 1952. Then he went to Changchun, and became a professor there in 1983. He taught at Sun Yat-Sen University since 1999.

Su was the Chairman of the Second International Conference on the Spectra of Rare Earth Elements, and a Committee Member of the Third and Sixth International Conferences on f-elements.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sysu.edu.cn/2012/en/academics/academics03/226.htm|title=Su Qiang|website=Sun Yat-Sen University}}</ref>
